uncited: Computes the exact Euclidean distance from a query point to the boundary of an axis-aligned rectangle centered at the origin.
It serves as a fundamental primitive for distance-field ray marching, allowing for efficient collision detection and rendering of rectangular shapes without polygonal approximation.
It is the 2D analog of the [Signed Box Distance Function](1092-signed-box-distance-function.md).
The rectangle spans $[-hsize_x, hsize_x] \times [-hsize_y, hsize_y]$.
Positive if outside, negative if inside, zero on the boundary.
where $|p|$ applies the absolute value component-wise to $p$.
where $\max(dv, 0)$ applies the maximum operator to each component of $dv$ with $0$, and $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean length.
This captures the distance to the closest edge when the point is inside the rectangle.
For unit-aligned grids, $hsize$ might be $(0.5, 0.5)$ for a $1 \times 1$ rectangle.
- **Degenerate Input:** If $hsize$ contains zero or negative values, the geometry is invalid or degenerate.
The formula assumes $hsize_x, hsize_y > 0$.

Very fast evaluation makes it suitable for real-time ray marching.
Rotated or skewed rectangles require transformation of the query point $p$ into the rectangle's local space before applying the function.
- **When to use:** Ideal for rendering simple rectangular shapes, UI elements, or grid-based structures in ray marching.
- **When not to use:** For complex curved surfaces or non-axis-aligned rectangles where transformation overhead outweighs benefits, or when higher-order primitives are needed.
The Signed Distance Function for rectangles is a standard primitive in the field of ray marching and implicit surface rendering.
